title: Reel 4: Fazola stories, Bebe, and Henry Raymond's jealousy
summary: Sal recalls working with Fazola at the Greenland, and Henry Raymond arguing about Fazola's solo.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: The women there, there were a bunch of characters, they said the Broken Dishes there. The Broken Dishes? That was her name. I had Fazola's applause with Bebe.
You better put down those tails, it's going on in the park, you know. It's alright.
It's too late now to worry about Fazola.

That's right, we'll see now. You know, it's a funny thing about Fazola. We used to start playing in the band, we used to double there all the time, see. And we used to have a little broad name Bebe. She was like a midget, see. But I had quite a few there. I can't remember.
I think I could wash the clothes.
Oh, I'm a child, I quit talking.

I'm talking about music. No, we had Fazola's, I'm about Fazola's. I used to go out all the time one day, it's me and Fazola's. You know, it's a funny thing, this is not about women. You know, some people are jealous of other people. So I don't have anything. But thank God that I'm not jealous about anything that anybody else is. Which is a good thing, it won't go away with it. You know, I was playing Fazola at the Greenland, see. And he had played Tony with his picture, you see there with Charlie Duke. And Tony was crazy about Fazola, man. And I just left Faz out there because they only closed the joint up. So I had Raymond ask me to go play with him out there, see. So Faz says, will you go out there? He says, and after a while I'll have my band there. I said, fine. So anyhow, I was still playing out there. Had some time ago there. The boy once, when I went to the newspaper, the Fazola had died, man. And then the picture and the paper, and Henry was jealous of Fazola. He said to me, well I guess he's not not playing the Munchie the Bobcats, but the devil, man. I said, man, I would say that to me. I would say that. Then he said to me, do you think that Fazola playing the solo of Munchie the Bobcats? I said, well, Henry, I know you're a fire musician. You're a clarinet player. I don't even play clarinet. He said, you're trying to tell me this mighty mad luck. I don't know what you're wrong. I said, mighty mad luck had a thin tone. He didn't have a tone like Faz said. And if you say it's mighty mad luck, I said, man, you already have a bad ear. So it wasn't too much long after that. He dies. I was in the band, man. And his son took his place, Lenny. Lenny died too. Lenny Raymond? Yeah, he died.
